<description>
Migrating a legacy wallet that holds no spendable material fails whenever the
wallet contains transactions. `migratewallet` returns
`std::bad_function_call (-1)` and the wallet is left unmigrated.

Two defects are involved, and the first one hides the second.

### 1. The migration check reads in-memory state that has not been updated yet

When the wallet being migrated has no spendable material,
`CWallet::ApplyMigrationData()` asserts that nothing is left behind in it:

```cpp
if (!m_address_book.empty()) return util::Error{_("Error: Not all address book records were migrated")};
if (!mapWallet.empty()) return util::Error{_("Error: Not all transaction records were migrated")};
```

The two checks look symmetric but are not. `DelAddressBookWithDB()` erases from
`m_address_book` straight away, so the first check sees current state.
`RemoveTxs()` only erases the transaction records from disk; it defers the
`mapWallet` removal to the db txn's `on_commit` listener, which does not run
until the txn is committed — after `ApplyMigrationData()` has returned.

`mapWallet` is therefore never empty at that point and the check always fails.

### 2. Aborting the txn calls a callback that was never set

`DbTxnListener` declares `on_commit` and `on_abort` as plain `std::function`
members and callers may set only the one they need. `RemoveTxs()` does exactly
that: `on_commit` is set, `on_abort` is left empty.

`TxnCommit()` and `TxnAbort()` each invoked their listener's callback
unconditionally, so the abort triggered by the failed check above threw
`std::bad_function_call`. The exception escaped the wallet entirely, replacing
the real error with an unhelpful one and skipping the caller's cleanup path.

### Fix

The first commit skips callbacks that are not set, and documents that they are
optional. The second discounts the transactions already queued for deletion
instead of requiring `mapWallet` to be empty.

They are kept separate because the second defect masks the first: with only the
listener fix applied, the migration surfaces the real error
`Error: Not all transaction records were migrated (-4)` instead of
`std::bad_function_call (-1)`.

### Testing

`src/wallet/test/db_tests.cpp` gains a regression test covering a listener with
only one callback set, for both commit and abort. It fails on master with
`std::bad_function_call` and passes with the fix.

`test/functional/wallet_migration.py` gains a case migrating a blank legacy
wallet with a watch-only address that has received a transaction. The test is
taken from #36483.

To reproduce on master, apply the functional test alone and run
`wallet_migration.py`.

Fixes #36483
</description>

<commits>
72889f7e1e wallet: skip unset db txn listener callbacks

DbTxnListener declares on_commit and on_abort as plain std::function
members and callers may set only the one they need. RemoveTxs() does
exactly that: it registers a listener with on_commit set and on_abort
left empty.

TxnCommit() and TxnAbort() invoked both unconditionally, so aborting a
db txn in which RemoveTxs() had run threw std::bad_function_call. The
exception escaped the wallet, replacing the error that caused the abort
with an unhelpful "std::bad_function_call" RPC error and skipping the
caller's cleanup path.

Skip callbacks that are not set, and document that they are optional.

50f254e53a wallet: fix migration of watch-only wallets

When the wallet being migrated has no spendable material,
ApplyMigrationData() asserts that no records are left behind in it. The
address book half of that check works because DelAddressBookWithDB()
erases from m_address_book straight away. The transaction half cannot:
RemoveTxs() only erases the records from disk and defers the mapWallet
removal to the db txn's on_commit listener, which runs after
ApplyMigrationData() has returned.

mapWallet is therefore never empty at that point, so migrating a
watch-only wallet that has transactions always failed with
"Error: Not all transaction records were migrated".

Discount the transactions queued for deletion instead.
</commits>
